title: Natural Weaving
strapline: Threading leaves, grasses and wool through a fence or frame — slow, absorbing outdoor art made from what nature gives.
intent: Children develop fine-motor control, patience and the pincer grip through the fiddly, rewarding work of weaving.
Children create collaborative and individual art from natural, found materials, connecting craft with the outdoors.
Children explore pattern, colour, texture and over-under sequence in a hands-on, three-dimensional way.
Children experience slow, calming, absorbing creativity — the antidote to a busy, fast day.
Children look closely at natural materials and make aesthetic choices about how to arrange them.
implementation: Set up a large shared loom on a fence or between two posts, warped with string or wool, so several children can weave together.
Provide a basket of natural weavables — long grasses, leaves, feathers, ribbon, wool, bendy twigs, flower stems.
Demonstrate the over-under motion once, then let children find their own rhythm — the technique comes with doing.
Offer individual hand-held frames — a forked stick or a cardboard loom — for children who want their own small piece.
Go on a gathering walk first: choosing and collecting the materials is part of the art and the looking.
Let the weaving grow and change over days as a communal outdoor artwork, adding to it as the seasons offer new materials.
key_questions: Can you take the grass over, then under, then over?
Which colours and textures will you choose next?
How does this leaf feel compared to that feather?
What pattern is your weaving making?
Where shall we find more natural materials to add?

impact.text: Children thread, weave and use one-handed movements with growing control and precision.
Children make choices about colours, materials and textures, and create with intent.
Children copy, continue and create simple over-under patterns and talk about them.
Children explore natural materials closely with all their senses.
Children stay with a fiddly, absorbing task and feel the satisfaction of finishing.

enhancements: A seasonal weaving — blossom and grasses in spring, gold leaves in autumn — changing with the year.
Hand-held cardboard or forked-stick looms so children can take their weaving with them.
A colour-themed weaving day: gather and weave only reds, or only greens.
Adding wool, ribbon and beads alongside the natural finds for texture contrast.
A gathering walk with bags, making the collecting of materials part of the project.

playing_exploring: Children explore the textures, colours and flexibility of natural materials as they weave.
Choosing and gathering materials invites open, sensory-rich exploration.
active_learning: The slow, fiddly work rewards patience and persistence, weave by weave.
Children set their own creative goals and stay with them to completion.
creating_thinking: Children plan patterns and colour combinations, holding a design in mind.
They solve the over-under problem and find their own weaving rhythm and solutions.
